title: Vision Genomics Portal
bodyHtml:
About the Portal

The VisionGenomics (Visualization and Inspection of Ocular Genetics and Functional Genomics) Knowledge Portal enables browsing, sharing, and exploring of human genetic association data with glaucoma, intraocular pressure, and in the future other ocular diseases and traits in relation to gene expression, genetic regulation, and epigenetic data in ocular and non-ocular tissues.

The goal is to enhance hypothesis testing, exploration and discovery of potential causal mechanisms, genes, and pathways for glaucoma and other ocular diseases.

Genetic regulation and chromatin accessibility data for the human optic nerve head, macula, and conventional and uveoscleral aqueous humor outflow pathway tissues will be added soon! 

Available Pages

To explore genome-wide associations with primary open angle glaucoma (POAG) in the context of peripheral retina expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs), GTEx eQTLs and splicing QTLs (sQTLs) in 49 tissues (v8), and human retina open chromatin regions in bulk and single cell tissue go to SignalSifter. eQTLs, sQTLs and open chromatin regions for the human optic nerve head, macula, trabecular meshwork/Schlemms’ Canal and ciliary body will be added soon.

To browse colocalization analysis results between POAG and intraocular pressure (IOP) genome-wide association study (GWAS) loci and retina eQTLs and GTEx v8 e/sQTLs go to Colocalization summary for a summary of the results by locus, and to eCAVIAR colocalizations and enloc colocalizations for GWAS locus by QTL type, target gene, and tissue combination based on the eCAVIAR and enloc methods, respectively.

Two sample Mendelian Randomization results between retina eQTLs or GTEx v8 e/sQTLs and POAG and IOP loci can be browsed at Mendelian Randomization.

All tables can be downloaded here: Downloads.

This portal includes supplementary tables that accompany the publication:

Integrating genetic regulation and single-cell expression with GWAS prioritizes causal genes and cell types for glaucoma.

Hamel AR, et al. Nat Commun. 2024 Jan 9;15(1):396. doi: 10.1038/s41467-023-44380-y.

PMID: 38195602.
